headline: NVIDIA Slides 6.34% as Chip Rally Euphoria Fades and Drags the Nasdaq Lower
body_html:
NVIDIA fell 6.34% in early trading as the enthusiasm behind its sharp rebound wore off. Commentary is asking whether the Nvidia-led rally really marked a market bottom, and the answer so far looks like maybe not. Chief executive Jensen Huang's return to the helm was greeted warmly inside the company, but coverage stresses that investigations and risks remain. Prices are not final.

The selling spread across the chip sector, where the average semiconductor stock fell 5.64%. AMD dropped 10.14%, Micron 8.82%, Arm 6.82%, Broadcom 4.51% and TSMC 3.56%. The Nasdaq fell 1.47% and the S&P 500 fell 0.49%. Outside chips the market held up better: 356 stocks rose and 296 fell among the 656 we track. Healthcare led the sectors, up 1.61% on average, followed by consumer discretionary at 1.28% and financials at 0.69%. Abercrombie Fitch was the standout mover, up 22.17%.

Through the day, watch whether NVIDIA steadies or whether the chip selling deepens, and whether the retail and healthcare strength keeps the broader market from sliding further. Oil, which recently touched three-month lows, is also on the radar.

briefs.headline: Chip leaders retreat together
briefs.body: The sell-off reached well beyond NVIDIA. AMD fell 10.14%, Arm 6.82%, Broadcom 4.51% and TSMC 3.56%. Broadcom had already been in focus after a recent scare over rival chip designs, and the early pattern suggests investors are trimming the whole AI hardware group at once.

briefs.headline: Retailers steal the spotlight
briefs.body: Apparel and sporting-goods names led the gainers. Abercrombie Fitch jumped 22.17%, Dick's Sporting Goods rose 14.13% and Burlington Stores gained 8.04%. The strength helped push consumer discretionary up 1.28% on average, making it the second-best sector this morning.

briefs.headline: Healthcare tops the sector table
briefs.body: Healthcare was the strongest sector, up 1.61% on average. Sanofi rose 8.55% and MiniMed gained 6.91%. With chips under pressure, defensive and medical names are drawing buyers, though morning moves can fade before the close.

briefs.headline: Memory makers take a hit
briefs.body: Micron fell 8.82% and Sandisk fell 9.18%. Commentary has been questioning how smaller AI models could weigh on future demand for memory, even as Micron's recent rally and buyback have drawn debate over how much upside is left.

briefs.headline: Chip-equipment names sell off hard
briefs.body: Semtech fell 12.19%, Ichor 11.61% and FormFactor 9.12%, all among the steepest declines. BE Semiconductor Industries bucked the trend, rising 10.44%. The split shows that selling in the supply chain is not uniform.

briefs.headline: Oil stays on watch
briefs.body: Energy shares fell 0.65% on average. Oil recently touched three-month lows before recovering on a threat to the Strait of Hormuz, and crude remains sensitive to Middle East headlines. Traders will watch whether that rebound holds as the session develops.
